t:
(a) Bonus Under Nurse Officer Candidate Accession Program.—Section 2130a(a)(1) of title 10, United States Code, is amended—
        (1) by striking “$10,000” and inserting “$20,000”; and 
        (2) by striking “$5,000” and inserting “$10,000”.  
    (b) Monthly Stipend Under Nurse Officer Candidate Accession Program.—Section 2130a(a)(2) of title is amended by striking “of not more than $1,000” and inserting “in an amount not to exceed the stipend rate in effect under section 2121(d) of this title”. 
    (c) Monthly Stipend for Students in Nursing or Other Health Professions Under Health Professions Stipend Program.—Section 16201(e)(2)(A) of title is amended by striking “stipend of $100 per month” and inserting “monthly stipend in an amount not to exceed the stipend rate in effect under section 2121(d) of this title”.

fable.w: This section only amends dollar amounts for bonuses and monthly stipends under military nurse and health professions programs. The words "Program" and "Accession" might hint at involvement of outside individuals, but they are benefit recipients, not participants in a federal decision. There is no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue.

qwen_block.w: This section amends statutory provisions regarding the monetary amounts of bonuses and stipends for nurse officer candidates and health professions students. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties before a federal decision is made. The changes are purely financial adjustments to existing programs.
qwen_block.s: Section 2130a(a)(1) of title 10, United States Code, is amended— (1) by striking “$10,000” and inserting “$20,000”; and (2) by striking “$5,000” and inserting “$10,000”.

opus.w: This section only changes bonus and stipend amounts for military nurse officer candidates and health professions students. The word "Program" and the payments to students might look like participation, but they are benefits paid to people who enroll, and applying for or receiving benefits does not count. Nothing here requires the federal government to consult with, hear from, or be sued by anyone outside the government before making a decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends statutory provisions regarding the dollar amounts of bonuses and stipends for military nurse candidates and health profession students. These are adjustments to federal benefit programs. The definition explicitly states that participation 'does not include applications for benefits or grants.' There is no requirement for the government to consult with, coordinate with, or receive input from outside parties (such as the students, nurses, or their representatives) before making these changes. The actors involved are Congress (amending the law) and the military (administering the program), all of which are inside the federal government.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing stipend amounts affects students or nurses (outside parties), so it involves them. However, the definition explicitly excludes "applications for benefits or grants." Adjusting the monetary value of a benefit program is an internal administrative or legislative change, not a process of consulting with or coordinating with outside parties before a decision is made. The section contains no mechanism for public comment, advisory boards, or consultation with states/tribes.
